patients.notes_about_rescue: Finder contacted on 4/17 attempting to get the squirrel to us. We found transport, but finder was no longer able to meet transporter that day and informed us he would contact the following day. We contacted him several times, left voice messages, and texted him on 4/18 with no response that day, nor over the weekend. Finder contacted today (4/22) informing that "work and family stuff were crazy last week," but today could meet a transporter to bring the squirrel to us. Per finder, squirrel has been sleeping/mostly staying in a kennel/storage room since 4/17 but finder lets squirrel out to roam and climbs on finder, which results in "scratches," but no intentional scratching. Finder notes the squirrel has "put its teeth to his hand" and "nibbled" on his hand, but no confirmed true bites or licks. Finder lives alone, but notes he had a friend over recently and also climbed on friend and friend was petting the squirrel bare handed. This squirrel also apparently was "nose to nose" with the finder's neighbor's dog, but denies any bites, licks, or scratches between the dog and squirrel. Informed finder of potential diseases (eg, leptospirosis, rabies, etc.) spread by squirrels and to F/U with his regular healthcare provider if he has any concerns or develops any abnormal symptoms.

patients.notes_about_rescue: Finder (Mary Redmon) called around 9AM today reporting a skunk was found in a water pipe (about 5 feet deep) under their porch, as the lid had become loose. The finder notes she smelled a skunk and heard crying coming from under their porch, then opened the hatch of their porch and saw the skunk sitting at the bottom of the pipe. Prior to calling the Center, the finder had placed a plank of wood with a towel attached to the end to offer a potential source of climbing/escape for the skunk. Since Shenandoah Co. Animal Control was unable to respond to this, Alysa, Rena (edu fellow) and Sydney (rehab fellow) did go out to rescue this skunk (used a catch pole & gloved hands). Upon getting ready to leave, I did call Mary to ensure the skunk was still there, which it was, but Mary informed me that her daughter, Julia Redmon, had touched the towel that was on the stick  with bare hands, did not immediately wash her hands, then may have eaten something, and that their neighbor, Jim White, also touched the towel with bare hands. I informed them that they should report to the Shenandoah Co HD/Lord Fairfax Health District (since after hours) to determine the best course of action, but that they should immediately wash their hands thoroughly and ensure to only handle the towel with gloved hands. She notes they do have a dog, but that the dog did not come into contact with the towel, so I advised that any people who touched the towel to not touch the dog until washing hands thoroughly due to risk of distemper, rabies, etc. I recommended that anything the skunk touched be handled only with gloves, double bagged w/ trash bags, and discarded. Additionally, I recommended that they follow-up with their medical provider for any urgent concerns regarding zoonotic diseases while awaiting response from the Health Department. The Admission and Supplemental Mammal Form was filled out over the phone with Mary; she reported that there was no bare skin contact between the skunk and any people, nor any bites, licks, or scratches by the skunk, and no interactions with domestic animals.
